name: Craniosynostosis-Dandy-Walker Malformation-Hydrocephalus Syndrome
aliases: Craniosynostosis with Dandy-Walker Malformation and Hydrocephalus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Craniosynostosis-Dandy-Walker Malformation-Hydrocephalus Syndrome

criteria.description: Premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures confirmed by imaging
Presence of Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by hypoplasia or agenesis of the cerebellar vermis, cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle, and enlargement of the posterior fossa
Evidence of communicating or non-communicating hydrocephalus on neuroimaging
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Characteristic craniofacial abnormalities including frontal bossing and midface hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of craniosynostosis, Dandy-Walker malformation, and hydrocephalus confirmed by imaging studies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging findings combined with clinical craniofacial assessment.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biochemical markers identified
imaging: CT or MRI showing premature cranial suture fusion
MRI demonstrating Dandy-Walker malformation features (cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, enlarged fourth ventricle)
genetic: No consistent single gene mutation identified; possible sporadic or multifactorial etiology
other: Clinical craniofacial examination revealing characteristic dysmorphic features

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and fourth ventricle cyst without cranial suture fusion
Craniosynostosis without associated Dandy-Walker malformation or hydrocephalus
Presence of other syndrome-specific features (e.g., Apert, Crouzon syndromes)
Hydrocephalus without craniosynostosis or posterior fossa malformations
Different etiology such as aqueductal stenosis or infection

redFlags: Rapidly increasing head circumference in infancy
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (vomiting, irritability, bulging fontanelle)
references: Kimonis VE, et al. Craniosynostosis syndromes. In: GeneReviews. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
Barkovich AJ, et al. Pediatric Neuroimaging. 5th ed. Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2012.
